analysis.title: U.S. Equities Color: UNCH (28 Oct 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +28bps at 7,744 with a $1.3bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX +55bps at 29,813, R2K +15bps at 2,823, Dow +19bps at 52,476. Volume was 16.606bn shares vs a YTD daily average of 18.494bn.

Equities were flat-to-higher as several overhangs cleared: the META and SPCX capital raises, better overnight tech prints (SKHY, VRT), ORCL (+10%) reaffirming its 2027 guide at its investor day, and a Fed meeting that was a non-event.

MSFT rose 4% after hours on a beat. Total revenue grew 19% y/y vs 17% y/y cc last quarter. Azure grew 48%, up from 43% last quarter, but the desk notes this is before the re-segmentation, so it is not comparable.
GOOGL fell 7% after hours. Cloud growth was solid, but Search growth of +12% vs +14% expected is likely to feed a share-loss narrative.

Flow: the desk saw early signs of demand in AI/Semis after 2-3 weeks of little buying, mostly from the long-only community. Activity elsewhere was muted. Asset managers and hedge funds were small net buyers. The desk rated floor activity 4 on a 1-10 scale.

FOMC held the fed funds target range at 3.75-4.00%. Governor Cook and President Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp hike. The statement kept inflation 'elevated' and upgraded economic activity to 'strong' from 'solid'.

Derivatives: a quiet session for the vol desk. S&P and NDX vol were offered across the curve and skew eased slightly. Call volumes are above the YTD average, and short-dated tech upside buying is picking up in outright calls and call spreads.
The desk continues to prefer NDX over S&P for upside expressions, using call spreads. Long dealer gamma concentrated to the topside is keeping the S&P in its recent range.
Implied move into the election is low, with a 1.24% straddle priced to next Tuesday's close.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held rates as expected, with two dissents in favor of a 25bp hike, which points to a hawkish bias in the committee.
The yield was unchanged on the day, at a level above 5%.
WTI rose 139bps on the day and remains above $100.

crypto_views: Bitcoin rose 115bps to $81,584 at the 10/28 close.
